paper.title: Are Large Language Models Good Classifiers? A Study on Edit Intent Classification in Scientific Document Revisions
paper.authors: Qian Ruan, Ilia Kuznetsov, Iryna Gurevych

label_definition_source.title: Re3: A Holistic Framework and Dataset for Modeling Collaborative Document Revision (Ruan, Kuznetsov, Gurevych), ACL 2024, pages 4635-4655
label_definition_source.used: Table 15 edit intent definitions (p. 4655), Table 11 EIC prompt (p. 4652), Section 5 add/delete observation (p. 4639)
label_definition_source.code_repo: https://github.com/UKPLab/re3 @ a312f93819e193c678af965d2cd161534ff7f59b (inspected only; not needed for the split)

source.fields: edit_index, id (node_ix_src===node_ix_tgt), doc_name, node_ix_src (new sentence id), node_ix_tgt (old sentence id), text_src (new sentence; empty for deletions), text_tgt (old sentence; empty for additions), label
source.split_provenance: The paper's fine-tuning scripts load exactly these three CSVs (tasks/task_data_loader.py: load_dataset('csv', keep_default_na=False); test_type='test'). The full Re3-Sci release on TUdatalib (https://tudatalib.ulb.tu-darmstadt.de/handle/tudatalib/4300) was not downloaded: it is behind a bot challenge for curl and is not needed, since the split files are in the paper's code repo.

frozen.fields: id (re3sci-test-<edit_index>), edit_index, pair_id (release `id`), doc_name, node_ix_old, node_ix_new (not sent to Jev), old_text (= text_tgt), new_text (= text_src), edit_action (derived: Modify if both non-empty, Add if old empty, Delete if new empty), gold (= label). File order preserved; verified identical to the authors' pandas keep_default_na=False loading.

test_n_resolution: Test N = 2,312, exactly as stated in the EMNLP paper Section 4.1 (p. 15053: 'training, validation, and test sets with 7,478/1,776/2,312 edits'). Train 7,478 and val 1,776 also match; total 11,566 = paper's 'comprises 11,566 high-quality human-labeled sentence edits from 314 document revisions'. Splits are document-disjoint (206/46/62 documents; 0 shared doc_name between test and train or val). Test docs: 37 NLPeer ARR-22 papers (1,495 edits) + 25 F1000RD papers (817 edits).

english_verification.metadata: Re3-Sci is built from F1000RD (F1000Research, English-language journal) and the ARR-22 subset of NLPeer (ACL Rolling Review submissions, English); neither paper mentions other languages.
english_verification.method: langid (all languages enabled) on every non-empty test sentence (3,696 texts: 2,035 new + 1,661 old); regex scan for characters outside Latin/Greek/math/punctuation blocks; all flagged texts inspected.
english_verification.result: 3,661/3,696 texts classified 'en'. The 35 non-'en' flags (la 14, it 9, da 2, es 2, ro 2, de/sv/fi/el/no/fr 1 each) are all English: short section headings ('Experiments', 'Implementation Details.', 'Data availability', 'Seurat interaction'), citation-heavy sentences, and math/unit-heavy sentences. The single non-Latin-script hit is a LaTeX-extraction glyph in an English sentence ('(j ̸= k)'). No non-English or code-mixed rows; no rows dropped.

data_checks.addition_deletion_labels_in_train_val: Add/Delete items in train+val (3,398) are only Fact/Evidence, Claim or Other (0 Grammar, 0 Clarity)

deviations: None from the released test split: all 2,312 edits, verbatim text, released gold labels.

Jev sees the same text-only input as the paper's classifiers (old sentence, new sentence), plus an explicit edit_action field (Modify/Add/Delete) derived deterministically from which side is empty; no document context (the paper's models get none).

Additions/deletions (928 test items) are asked with a three-label question (Fact/Evidence, Claim, Other) instead of all five labels. Justification is a priori: Re3 Section 5 (p. 4639) states sentence additions/deletions 'are never intended for superficial language enhancement', the Grammar/Clarity definitions describe changes to existing wording, and 0/3,398 train+val additions/deletions carry Grammar or Clarity. Metrics are still computed over all five labels on all 2,312 items.
